_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4513 (branch fix/4513-updateproperty-empty-value) — `createUpdatePropertyService` (service_call `updateProperty`, the THIRD writer of a frontmatter key) refuses a value that IS the empty string. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). ⛔ The SUBJECT lives in `packages/services/src`, the AXES in `packages/cli/tests` — on purpose: no workflow runs jest for `packages/services` (`test-ci-batched.sh` drives exactly three configs — obsidian-plugin, cli, core — and CI touches the package only via `npm run build -w @kitelev/exocortex-services`), so axes placed beside the subject would sit outside every gate. The services suite itself is HEALTHY (57/57 on 474e9dd5) — unreachable, not broken. `packages/cli/jest.config.js` is run whole by the required `test-coverage-cli` and maps `@kitelev/exocortex-services` to the package SOURCE, so the mutated copy is what the axes exercise. The harness runs the new axes TOGETHER with the two pre-existing cli suites that import the same package, so a guard that was too broad surfaces as a RED CONTROL instead of passing unnoticed.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/services/src/grounding-service-factories.ts

M1_empty_value_guard_removed._note: #4513 primary item. Neutralises the refusal on a value that IS the empty string, restoring the junk write (`prop: ""` that looks like a cleared property). The mutation is TYPE-PRESERVING (same `value === <string literal>` shape, a sentinel that can never arrive) rather than `if (false)`, so a compile failure cannot be mistaken for a vacuous axis (ITRV §A36/§A97). Predicted V1 V2 — they redden together BY CONSTRUCTION: V1 pins that the refusal is TOTAL (nothing written) and V2 that the message is diagnosable; one guard carries both. V4 stays green and is the LOAD-BEARING control for the opposite direction — it proves the refusal keys on the empty string and not on whitespace. V3/V5/V6 stay green: they restate the pre-existing contract, which this mutant does not touch.

M2_guard_widened_to_trim._note: The TOO-BROAD half of the same guard: widening the strict `=== ""` into a trim() test. Predicted V4 ALONE: the refusal axes V1/V2 pass either way (an empty string trims to itself), so only the whitespace control notices. ⛔ The REASON differs from the `property_set` twin in #4511, and the difference was measured here rather than inherited (2026-10-02). That twin argues a trimming predicate would make the live whitespace carriers unwritable; through THIS factory it would not, because this path cannot write them at all: `updateProperty` calls `serializeValue` with the default `quoteScalars=false`, so a raw `" "` lands as `key: ` + spaces and js-yaml reads it back as NULL, while the 5 live `exo__DisplayNameSpec_separator` carriers are all QUOTED (`" "`, `" · "`) — a form this serializer cannot emit — and `" · "` would survive trim() anyway (three characters). V4 therefore pins the PREDICATE (no trimming), not a use case, and strict stays on the narrower true ground: it refuses strictly less than a trimming predicate and matches both sibling writers byte for byte.
